subject: Insurance
title: Regulatory Stress Tests
description: A 60-second lesson on Regulatory Stress Tests.

hook.text: Regulators force insurers to prove they can survive a 1-in-200-year disaster.

buildup.text: Solvency II in Europe requires insurers to hold enough capital to survive a 99.5% confidence level of losses.

discovery.text: Stress tests simulate extreme scenarios: a pandemic plus an earthquake plus a market crash.

twist.text: Some argue stress tests create false confidence. If the 1-in-200-year event is wrong, the test is meaningless.

climax.text: Stress tests are imperfect but indispensable.

quiz.question: What do regulatory stress tests require insurers to demonstrate?
options: Ability to survive extreme disaster scenarios
